combo_46c71ad48968.summary: The components are generally compatible for a basic robotic arm build, but powering the servos directly through the Arduino or breadboard is a significant risk.
notes: Do not power the MG996R and SG90 servos directly from the Arduino 5V pin, as current draw under load will reset the board; use the external 5V 5A power supply directly to the servo
The 5V output from the power supply is slightly below the 4.8V-7.2V operating range if accounting for voltage drop under heavy load, though generally functional for standard operat
Breadboard power rails may not handle the high surge currents of the MG996R servo under stall conditions; direct wiring to a distribution bus is recommended.

combo_aecc6c32053b.summary: The system components are generally well-matched for a 12V architecture, but require careful power routing and mechanical reinforcement.
notes: Ensure the power switch rating (0.5A) is not exceeded by total motor stall current, as the TB6612FNG can peak at 3.2A.
Using a breadboard for high-current motor connections can cause voltage drops and unstable operation; solder connections are recommended.
Acrylic frames are brittle under impact; ensure proper mounting torque and consider PLA or thicker acrylic for the LQR balancing robot chassis.

combo_398826970278.summary: The core components are conceptually well-matched for BLDC FOC control, but careful attention is needed regarding logic voltage conversion and MCU power provisioning.
notes: A 5V or 3.3V step-down regulator (BEC) is required to safely power the STM32 and sensors from the 11.1V (3S) Li-ion pack.
Verify that the 3-phase BLDC driver accepts 3.3V PWM logic levels and matches the peak current draw of the outrunner motor.
The AS5600 encoder over I2C has bandwidth and latency limitations that can restrict maximum motor speed during FOC closed-loop operation.

TP4056 charger module safely supports charging the 1S LiPo battery from a 5V USB source.
